parameters.name: Short Interest
parameters.value: Short interest 12.06% of float (184.39M shares), though only 1.36% of total shares outstanding (float is a small slice of the company given SpaceX's large insider/founder ownership). Elevated float-based short interest for a recent IPO can reflect difficulty borrowing/hedging shares around lockup unlocks rather than pure bearish conviction, and could pose squeeze risk if sentiment turns positive.

parameters.name: Insider Activity
parameters.value: Net selling context: early investors and pre-IPO institutional holders are selling into a series of staggered lockup expirations running July-November 2026, largely attributed by commentary to portfolio-concentration management rather than negative views on the company. This is partly offset by mechanical index-fund buying as SpaceX's weight in the Nasdaq-100/Russell 1000/Morningstar indexes increases (~3.4x) with a mid-September rebalance; it is unclear whether this fully offsets sell pressure.

stocks.notes: SPCX (SpaceX) went public and began Nasdaq trading in 2026, so analyst coverage/history is comparatively short and price-target dispersion is wide. Short interest and insider-selling readings both likely reflect lockup-expiration mechanics specific to a new IPO rather than pure bearish sentiment — flagged as squeeze/technical risk rather than a fundamental negative signal.
